text:
Ryan McLeod played his 400th NHL game on Wednesday against the Rangers, a milestone the Buffalo News noted came after a slight detour. It arrives in the quietest stretch of his time in Buffalo: 1 goal and 4 points in 21 games after 54 points last season, with his ice time down almost two minutes a night over his last ten.

A lot of this is luck. The Sabres have scored 11.6 fewer goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice, one of the biggest gaps we track, and he's shooting under 6%. His own chances are down too, though, at 0.39 expected goals per 60 against 0.50 last season. The tools haven't gone anywhere. His top speed ranks in the 97th percentile, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on 61% of his entries and setting up 8.0 primary shot assists per 60. Evolving-Hockey did warn that his 2025-26 results ran ahead of his chances. Our numbers project about 30 points, which assumes the bounces start coming back.
headline: Ryan McLeod reaches 400 games in a cold stretch
